name: Liberty Blue
lede: Liberty Blue is a dark, slightly purplish blue first recorded in the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary, named for the word liberty for reasons no source consulted here explains.

sections.title: A 1930 blue
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary of color lists Liberty Blue on plate 44, swatch B10, first recorded in 1927, with the Munsell notation 6.7PB 3.0/7.2 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system files the same swatch as a moderate purplish blue, 5.2 units from that block's center [1]. Neither source says why the color carries the word liberty, and the reason is undocumented here [1].

Our library's nearest named neighbor is Coolie, a warm-grey blue only 2.7 units away, then Cyanine Blue and Imperial Blue, both about 3 units off [1]. The plain name [[liberty]] belongs to a brighter, more violet-leaning blue in the same library, not a darker relative of this one [1]. Liberty Blue sits closest in hue to [[cyanine-blue]] and [[imperial-blue]], two names from the same mid-century color dictionaries [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Liberty Blue covers at least five percent of the canvas in 70 works, about three tenths of one percent [2]. It peaks in the 1920s, in 5 of 237 paintings, seven times the archive's overall rate for that decade [2]. Vilhelm Lundstrøm carries it in four of his seventeen paintings here, eighty times the baseline rate, and Henri Matisse in four of fifty, twenty-seven times the baseline [2]. It shares a canvas with [[navy]] far more than chance would predict, fifty-six times the baseline [2]. These are computed color matches on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, never a pigment identification [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].

origin.named_after: undocumented; Maerz and Paul give no reason for the word liberty

questions.q: Which 1930 color dictionary first records Liberty Blue?

openers: Liberty Blue has carried its name since 1927, with no recorded reason why.
